thread:
Kara: ran into a repeat problem in today's load test: clients retried streaming sessions and we re-ran expensive decoding on the model cluster. cascade started when gateway hedging kicked in for perceived short timeouts.
Milo: can we avoid hedging for streams and still be safe for short requests?
Sanjay: yes — but we need reliable detection and a cheap resume mechanism. my thought: two levers: 1) explicit conn-type header from SDKs; 2) small embedded resume token with compact checkpoint info for legacy paths.
Irene: how compact? embedding full kv-checkpoint might be heavy. we could encode a short checkpoint fingerprint + offset and a Bloom-ish sketch to validate quickly.
Vik: hmm Bloom adds false positives. maybe a hybrid: signed opaque token that contains (model_hash, offset, short_kv_id) and an optional server-side cache when cross-node resume is required.
Kara: agree. also admission: requests (including retries) should consume per-route admission tokens. refill tokens only on success, not on timeout/failure, to avoid replenishing during surge.
Milo: +1. and add a small reserve slice for retries so common transient failures can still get a limited retry without starving new traffic.
Sanjay: propose API header flow:
- server returns `x-rw-resume-token: <token>` on first successful streaming handshake or on client request
- client sends token back as `x-rw-resume-token` when reconnecting
- gateway validates token locally (HMAC) or consults regional cache if token_id present
- if accepted respond `x-rw-resume-accepted: true` and `x-rw-resume-offset: N`
Irene: failure cases: token expired -> 410, model mismatch -> 409 with `resume_model_mismatch=true`, revoked -> 403. document these so SDKs can fall back cleanly.
Vik: admission config sketch (route manifest):
```yaml
route: /v1/stream
admission:
  tokens_capacity: 400
  retry_reserve_pct: 12
  refill_on_success: true
  stream_detection:
    opt_in_header: x-rw-conn-type
    heuristic_first_chunk_ms: 150
resume_policy:
  enabled: true
  embedded_ttl_s: 45
  replicated_ttl_s: 60 # optional redis backing for cross-node resume
  max_per_tenant: 500
```
Kara: another UX idea: when we enqueue for async processing because admission is exhausted, return 202 with `x-rw-queue-pos` so SDKs can show a queue position to end-users. that reduces blind retries.
Milo: love `x-rw-queue-pos`. but queue-pos is best-effort; must avoid leaking exact load for privacy. maybe quantized buckets like 1-10, 11-50, 51+.
Sanjay: important: hedging must be disabled whenever a valid resume token is present to avoid duplicate in-flight compute. also disable hedging for any connection marked streaming.
Irene: metrics to add: `resume_tokens_issued`, `resume_accepts`, `resume_rejects_model_mismatch`, `admission_tokens_used`, `retry_reserve_utilization`, `enqueue_rate`, `queue_pos_buckets`. dashboards + one alert: resume_rejects_model_mismatch >1% over 5m.
ops-bot: incident: duplicate-stream-compute spike detected at 2026-01-28T09:12:00Z, pages sent to #eng-sre.
Vik: rollout plan: feature-flag `edge.stream_resume_v1` + `edge.admission_refill_on_success`. start with internal-only models and a 0.5% external canary.
Kara: owners: Milo (gateway token & admission), Sanjay (resume encoding + security), Irene (telemetry + dashboards), Vik (SDK header + enqueue UX). I'll draft the RFC with sequence diagrams and failure modes.
Milo: I'll prototype token HMAC format and an in-memory LRU replicator for regional failover. will simulate node flip scenarios.
Sanjay: will add threat model: forged tokens, replay beyond TTL, and revoke signals on model rollout. recommend embedding token_id for optional revocation set lookup.
Irene: will wire traces so each request records `resume.token_present`, `resume.result`, `admission.tokens_before`, `admission.tokens_after`.
Vik: doc note: SDKs should expose a helper that automatically attaches token and falls back to fresh session on 410/409/403. will draft examples.
Kara: good. target spike + small canary in two weeks. add experiment docs and rollback criteria (enqueue_rate > 1% or resume_rejects_model_mismatch > 1%). :thumbsup:
